subject: DPA: roles, telemetry, and embeddings — redlines & signing timeline
messages:
From: Sara White <sara.white@acme.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acme.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: roles, telemetry, and embeddings — redlines & signing timeline

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As we start the procurement loop, legal ran into a few open items in the DPA draft that need clarification before we can execute:

- Controller vs Processor: the current draft is a bit ambiguous around embeddings (are embeddings considered "customer data" or a derived service output?).
- Logs & telemetry: our security team needs clear retention limits and what telemetry Redwood considers "operational" vs "diagnostic".
- Subprocessors: please confirm current list and provide the notification cadence for additions.
- Cross-border: we need to confirm the mechanism for transfers from EU to US (SCCs or alternative).

Can you share a redline and a short one-page summary mapping the above items to specific DPA clauses? Also let us know your preferred esign flow (DocuSign/AdobeSign) and whether you can target signature next week — we have a board approval window that closes 6 June.

Appreciate it,

Sara White
Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
sara.white@acme.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: procurement_requirements_0426.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara White <sara.white@acme.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: roles, telemetry, and embeddings — redlines & signing timeline

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal) and Rishi (privacy/security) to propose concrete language. Quick responses to your bullets before we send a redline: 

- Embeddings: our position is that embeddings generated from customer content are treated as "derivative outputs" used to serve the customer and are covered by the DPA; we can add explicit language that Redwood has no rights to sell or use embeddings for its own models.
- Logs & telemetry: we differentiate "operational telemetry" (routing/latency/error rates) and "diagnostic logs" (request traces, sample payloads). Operational telemetry will be retained for analytics as aggregated/anonymous by default; diagnostic logs that include customer prompts will be retained per contract or purged after X days — we'll propose specific retention windows in the redline.
- Subprocessors: we'll attach the current list and a 30-day notification clause for additions (with opt-out right for critical subprocessors).
- Cross-border: we support SCCs and can offer a DPA addendum for EU customers; Laura, please confirm the standard language.

I'll attach a redline draft and a one-page mapping and propose a 30-minute call Monday to close open items before your 6 June window. What times work for you?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0123

Attachments: ACME_DPA_redline_v2.docx (redline, tracked changes), subprocessor_list_20260530.csv (current subprocessors)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara White <sara.white@acme.com>, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA: roles, telemetry, and embeddings — redlines & signing timeline

Sara and Jordan — I've reviewed the DPA and prepared a redline + short summary. High-level points below (see attached ACME_DPA_redline_v2.docx and redline_summary_onepager.pdf):

1) Role definitions (Controller / Processor)
- Clause update: add definitional sentence: "For clarity, Customer is Controller of Customer Data; Redwood is Processor with respect to processing performed on behalf of Customer, except where Redwood independently determines aggregated telemetry for service improvement which is controlled by Redwood in anonymized form."
- Add explicit carve-out: "Embeddings derived from Customer Data are Processor outputs and not used by Redwood for model training or product benchmarking absent Customer's written consent."

2) Logs & telemetry
- Define "Operational Telemetry" vs "Diagnostic Logs."
- Proposed retention: Operational telemetry (aggregated metrics) — 24 months; Diagnostic logs containing customer content — default 90 days, option to extend to 12 months for enterprise customers.
- Access & audit: Security team can request audit traces with appropriate NDA/attestation.

3) Subprocessors
- Current list attached. We propose 30 days notice for new subprocessors and an escape right for material data residency changes.

4) Data transfers
- Proposed approach: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) + supplemental technical measures for EU customers. We can produce an addendum specific for Acme EMEA entities.

5) Execution flow
- We can execute via DocuSign (preferred) or AdobeSign. I attached a sample DocuSign envelope link in the Drive folder. If Acme is ready, we can prepare a signature-ready DPA with tracked redlines and route for signature next Tue/Wed.

I've included language suggestions and called out the one area where I expect back-and-forth: retention window for diagnostic logs in regulated EU cases. If Acme needs shorter retention, we can propose data-scoped configurations in Redwood Private or Dedicated.

Regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: redline_summary_onepager.pdf (summary of key clause edits)
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/dpa-redlines-acme

From: Sara White <sara.white@acme.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, legal@acme.com, dpo@globalsec.com
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 08:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: DPA: roles, telemetry, and embeddings — redlines & signing timeline

Laura / Jordan — thanks for the thorough redline. A few quick notes from Acme legal/security: 

- Embeddings: we appreciate the explicit carve-out. We still need a short sentence that these embeddings are "not personal data for purposes of GDPR when pseudonymized/aggregated" — happy to accept Redwood's language if you add that clause.
- Diagnostic logs retention: Acme's baseline is 90 days for US entities; for EU entities we require 30 days unless otherwise agreed. Can Redwood confirm a mechanism to set region-specific retention? (If not, we will ask for the 30-day limit in the EMEA addendum.)
- SCCs: please send the SCC text you intend to rely on and a suggested timeline for the EMEA addendum.

If Redwood can provide the SCC + a one-pager showing where retention is configured per-region, we'll be ready to move to DocuSign by Tue 2 June. HubSpot Deal ID: 12345.

Best,

Sara White
Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
